questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere, where there was a focus on the social life. I heard about the social offers that Uni of Glasgow had with sports clubs and societies. I also wanted to go somewhere, where I could explore the country and I speak the language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Glasgow was very helpful in answering all questions I had and also had a lot of offers in fresher's week for international students, i.e. a tour around the city and a mentor-program

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Difficult - there is a housing crisis. Most private student accommodations offer rooms for full year students only, meaning that you can only rent something for the entire academic year, semester 1 and 2. I found a place in the city centre through Unite Students - BUT start looking ASAP

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its difficult to find. But I enjoyed it, I got to meet other internationals. Usually, only freshers/1.years live in the uni halls (dorms), meaning they are around 17-18-19 years old. Living elsewhere made it easier to find friends closer to my own age.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was okay, the room was absolutely stripped of stuff - I had to buy everything from pillows, duvets, kitchen stuff and even a toilet brush. Prepare to spend some money on that. 
Also, if you can, find a place in the west end - most students live there and there is almost a little uni-town over there. If not, try the city centre, it is easy to get to the west end with the subway.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy, Glasgow Uni helped a lot

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: 2 week drop period at beginning of term, where I would be assigned to the pre-applied courses but I could change if necessary

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Uni is very helpful with answering questions. They are very fast during the drop period - I changed a course and it was super easy. They even reserved a spot on the course I wanted, without dropping me from the other one, while I was waiting for approval from Copenhagen

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for courses because they interest you and don't worry if they are not approved immediately, they are usually given right before or in the first week of term .

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: level 2,3 and 4

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: different from course to course and level to level - it depends on the course convenor. However, prepare to be more active in class - some professors cold calls a lot

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
jurisprudence, level 2
Principles of Healthcare law, level 3
Criminal law: theory and doctrine, level 4

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I took Jurisprudence partly because I read in previous reports that it was easy - the course was fine, but the exam was difficult, maybe because of a new exam type. However, the course was still good and the curriculum was easy

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The sportsmembership was more than expected. Also trips, and going out to eat a lot

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food - I didn't cook much

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Loved the clubs

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Too much to count :) So many clubs and societies and most of them had a social every week or every other week. Definitely worth joining a club or two

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: mountaineering club has different hiking trips every other week. Go to as many tasters as you can in the freshers week, so you can try the clubs

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Trips around the country! Rent a car (at Arnold clark) and drive to the islands! I saw northern lights on orkney.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes, people in Glasgow are super friendly - only the accent is a bit difficult

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go up and talk to strangers, they are very helpful and kind - especially at pubs :) go to the socials with the different uni clubs or just go out for a pint or two at the GUU beer bar (glasgow university union)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: not much, they are more open than the Danes

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and that they befriend you at parties. If you meet people at a party, they will often text you afterwards to meet up for coffee or something else to make friends with you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
pack for a rainy day (or 20) :)) 
Go on trips early in the semester, so you won't stress about exams 
go to different club socials

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything! I loved Glasgow :)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The accent - but even other Scots struggle with the Glaswegian accent :))

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
